01/06/2014

Dr Charles White
Thyroid Specialist
Bayview Private Hospital
81 Canyon Road
Bayview
Dear Dr White,

Re: Ms Lola Duval, DOB: 27/05/1990

I am writing to refer Ms Duval, a 24-year-old student, who is demonstrating features consistent
with Grave's disease. Your further assessment of her thyroid function and management would be
appreciated.

Regarding the medical history, Ms Duval had laryngitis in 2012. She suffers from anxiety and
insomia, for which she occasionally takes sleeping pills. Her family history is unremarkable for      Commented [M1]: insomnia
thyroid disorders.

Initially, Ms Duval presented on 31/05/2014 with a two-month history of tremors, palpitations,
diaphoresis and heat intolerance. Additionally, she reported that she had lost ten kg over the same
period of time. She was frustrated due to the weight loss, as her appetite was normal and her
eating habits have not changed. On examination, blood pressure and heart rate were slightly
elevated and her hands were trembling. Palpation revealed enlarged painless thyroid gland and on
eye examination she had exophthalmus. In view of the above, some tests were requested to              Commented [M2]: exophthalmos
confirm the provisional diagnosis.

Today, her test results came back. ECG findings indicated sinus arrythmia. Thyrois function test      Commented [M3]: arrhythmia
showed a significantly decreased level of TSH and elevated levels of free T3 and T4, which are        Commented [M4]: Thyroid
suggestive of hyperthyroidism. Ms Duval was advised to perform additional thyroid antobidy tests
                                                                                                      Commented [M5]: antibody
and thyroid scan.

Please, do not hesitate to contact me, if you have any queries.

Yours sincerely,
Doctor
